sources.entry: gitbucket - Git platform powered with easy installation, high extensibility & GitHub API compatibility (alternative to GitHub). (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Scala/Java
GitBucket | Git platform powered by Scala

summary.one_liner: GitBucket is a self-hostable Git web platform written in Scala, offering repository hosting, issues, pull requests, and a GitHub-compatible API.
summary.what_it_does: GitBucket provides public and private Git repositories accessible over HTTP/HTTPS and SSH, with GitLFS support. It includes a repository viewer with an online file editor, plus issues, pull requests, and a wiki for each repository. It also has an activity timeline, email notifications, and account and group management with LDAP integration. A plugin system extends functionality, and the README lists official plugins for gists, emoji, pages, and notifications. It is distributed as a gitbucket.war file that runs with java -jar or on a Servlet 3.0 container.
use_cases: self-host a private Git server for a team
host Git repositories with a web interface
run a GitHub-like issue tracker and pull requests on own server
manage user accounts and groups with LDAP
edit repository files online in a browser
deploy a Git platform on Tomcat or Jetty
how_to_run: Download the latest gitbucket.war from the releases page
Open the web UI and log in with root / root
Alternatively, deploy gitbucket.war to a Servlet 3.0 container such as Jetty or Tomcat
To upgrade, stop GitBucket, replace gitbucket.war, and start again; back up ~/.gitbucket first
notable: GitHub API compatibility, a stated top priority of the project
Plugin system with official gist, emoji, pages, and notifications plugins
Single WAR file install with default admin login
Data stored in ~/.gitbucket by default for simple backup
caveats: Does not support Jakarta EE yet
Release 4.47.0 and 4.48.0 include large database migrations; back up the database before upgrading
Upgrading from 4.42 or earlier to 4.43+ with the default H2 database requires a manual dump and restore
